stated_facts: The complainant boarded a Bandra local train yesterday afternoon.
An unknown individual secretly removed the complainant's Vivo mobile phone from their pocket.
The approximate value of the mobile phone is Rs. 15,000.
negated_events: No physical injury or bodily harm was suffered by the complainant.
No threat or intimidation was made by anyone.
inferred_facts: The non-consensual removal of the mobile phone from the complainant's pocket establishes dishonest intention (animus furandi) to cause wrongful gain to the perpetrator and wrongful loss to the complainant.
The act was an accomplished clandestine theft (pickpocketing) in a public transit setting.
missing_facts_to_clarify: Identity, physical description, or apprehension status of the suspect.
Whether the act was committed by an individual acting alone or as part of an organized syndicate or gang operating on railway routes.
Prior criminal record or conviction history of the perpetrator.
IMEI number, serial number, and purchase receipt of the mobile phone to facilitate tracing.
Current recovery or possession status of the stolen mobile phone.
recommended_action: The narrated facts disclose a prima facie offence of theft under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. Because the stated value of the stolen property is approximately Rs. 15,000 (exceeding the Rs. 5,000 threshold of the Section 303(2) proviso), the offence is classified as cognizable and non-bailable under Schedule I of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. The complainant should report the occurrence to the Government Railway Police (GRP) station having jurisdiction over Bandra, providing the IMEI number and invoice. The police may record the information under Section 173 BNSS, subject to any preliminary enquiry under Section 173(3) BNSS if deemed necessary, and proceed with investigation. If investigation establishes the involvement of an organized pickpocketing gang, Section 112 BNS may subsequently be added.

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: The essential ingredients of theft under Section 303 BNS are fully satisfied: the Vivo mobile phone is movable property, was in the possession of the complainant, and was moved out of the complainant's pocket without consent with inferred dishonest intention. Because the alleged value is approximately Rs. 15,000, the petty theft community service proviso under Section 303(2) does not apply.
statutory_elements_supported: Taking out of possession without consent
Moving of property in order to such taking
unestablished_elements: Prior conviction record of the perpetrator

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 112 BNS penalizes petty organised crime, explicitly referencing organised pickpocketing and theft in public transport systems. While the act took place on a local train, the statutory provision specifically requires the offence to be committed by 'organised criminal groups or gangs' or mobile groups creating a network of contacts. The narrative does not currently contain evidence linking the pickpocket to an organized group or syndicate.
statutory_elements_supported: Pickpocketing occurring in a public transport system
unestablished_elements: Commission by an organised criminal group, gang, or network

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS requires threatening another with injury to person, reputation, or property with intent to cause alarm. The complainant explicitly stated that no threat of any kind was given ('न ही किसी ने कोई धमकी दी'), directly negating the core ingredient.
unestablished_elements: Threat of injury to person, reputation, or property
Intent to cause alarm or compel any act/omission

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 114 BNS defines hurt as causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity. The narrative explicitly negates hurt or injury ('मुझे कोई चोट नहीं लगी'), making this section inapplicable.
unestablished_elements: Causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 97 BNS applies to kidnapping or abducting a child under ten years of age with intent to steal movable property. No child abduction or kidnapping is alleged.
unestablished_elements: Victim being a child under ten years of age

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 338 BNS relates to the forgery of valuable security, will, or authorities to transfer property. The matter involves physical pickpocketing of a phone, with no forged documents or securities involved.
unestablished_elements: Making a false document or forgery
Subject matter being a valuable security, will, or authority

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 345 BNS addresses the fraudulent use of a false property mark. There are no allegations regarding false marking of movable goods or receptacles.
unestablished_elements: Use of a false property mark

candidate_evaluations.reasoning: Section 35 BNS is a general exception providing the right of private defence of body and property. It defines a legal justification and does not constitute a substantive offence chargeable against an accused.
